Remove protection cover A and place it in a safe place until it is reused, taking care not to pull the safety pin of the cylinder valve
Fasten suspension arms B to the cylinder head

Introduction
This document explains the steps for replacing the CO2 cylinders when testing the system or when the automatic fire extinguishing system of the gas unit operates.
The CO2 automatic fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state at a pressure of approximately 80 bar. These cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area commensurate with the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas sprinklers and flame detectors distributed as in the following table:-
Flame detector | Heat detector | Sprinklers | Number of cylinders | 
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Right combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Left combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 8 | 7 | Oil tank
Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate, a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line; then the weight-release solenoid moves and the fire system operates. At the same time, the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow turning system operates. When the automatic fire extinguishing system operates, the cylinders are discharged, and in this case they are replaced.

Remove the plug from the cylinder valve opening and fit the high pressure hose E into the cylinder valve, taking care to place a Klingerit gasket to ensure a tight connection | 5.
